# Review (pass 1) — secret-history-121-124 (§§121–124)

Checked: all 68 units, 491 words. Mechanical checks (by script, passing before and after): word count per unit equals t; every t word equals the packet's romanized word; the first morph of every word ends in the packet's Ming gloss in brackets; no morph other than the first carries a bracket; `t`, the word count and unit boundaries were not touched. Edits were made to units.json in place by script (l, i, n, morph, and one sentence of `about`).

Severity counts: major 0, moderate 6, minor 37, trivial 7 (total 50 changes).

## Changes (unit · field · severity · what was wrong · what was done)

- U2 · i · minor · "never" overstates ülü + participle + büleġe (a plain negative, "were not ones to part"); no "never" in the form or the Ming.
- U3 · words[0] (word 21) morph · minor · žaγ̇arin was split into žaγ̇ari + "-n of uncertain force", yet the same part has the plural žaγ̇arid (n drops before -d, as qaγan → qād, ežen → ežed): an n-stem noun, no separate ending. Merged into one morph.
- U3 · n · minor · note matched to the morph fix above.
- U5 · i · trivial · "himself" has no word in the Mongol.

## Findings refused or left open (with reason)

- Ming typo 吉 at word 97 (žiγ̇aγsan-u): kept as printed in the gloss bracket; reading as 吿 'tell' confirmed by word 115 (吿了的). Drafter right.
- Ming typo 聰 at word 250 (qačar): drafter's 'cheek' kept. The earlier-part glossary already reads qačar as 'cheek' [腮], and 'fair-cheeked ladies' fits; 聰 'clever' has no fit. The bracket keeps the printed 聰. Drafter right.
- Ming 做漢 at word 232 (boluγ̇asu): slip for 做呵; noted in U30 n only, bracket kept as printed.
- Speakers at 105-112 (Temüjin, after 'Temüžin ügülerün') and 113-144 (Qorchi replying: 'nama-ji', 'the man who told'): kept. Speaker at 424-439 (Chinggis, unnamed, giving orders to three men with a plural imperative): kept as drafted; the i opens a quotation with no named speaker, which is honest. Speakers at 440-466 likewise.
- Subject of the 165-174 chain (U22): left as drafted ('those who had parted from Jamuqa … were camped'). The recap in U26 attaches the camping to Temüžin-i, so Temüjin as camper is as likely; i and n already state the doubt. Not changed because the form does not decide; remaining doubt.
- ba at 233 and 281: left as drafted (233 'we also—'; 281 joined to the preceding sentence although Shiratori's full stop falls before it). 281 could as well head the oath-clause 'ba qadqulduqui …'; no form decides. Remaining doubt.
- abča (46): left as 'ab- + -ča, ending of uncertain force'; the Ming 將來 suggests abči- 'bring' + -a, but nothing in the sources confirms it.
- žaγ̇arin: kept as 'divine sign'; reanalysed only as an n-stem (see U3, U11).
- bulun (223): reanalysed as a spelling of bolun (hedged), see U28.
- nereidčü (325): kept; matches the glossary entry for the same token (nere- + -id- + -čü), with the Ming here 名着.
- qadqulduqui (282): kept (qadqu- + -ldu- + -qui; Ming 厮殺的, 厮 = 'one another').
- qola-jin / oira-jin 'of the far / of the near' (461, 463) and the English 'qoqochaq of the far, odora of the near' in U62: the meaning of qola/oira is from the drafter's own knowledge, not from Shiratori or the Ming (which gives only 箭名), against the sole-source rule. Not changed: the n and the morph glosses say so openly. Remaining doubt; the owner may prefer i to leave the two words untranslated.
- Arrow names qoγ̇očaγ, odora: kept as untranslated names (Ming 箭名).
- aγsa- (335 etc.): kept; i 'took up the quiver' against l 'wore the quiver' is an interpretive step flagged in n; not changed.
- Taičiγ̇udai (448): kept as a clan epithet of Qutu; n now gives the reason (the count 'three'). The glossary has Taičiγ̇udai as a man's name [人名]; the glosser must broaden it with Ming 種名.
- Nekün-Taishi, Daritai-Ödchigin, Ögölei-Cherbi, Süiketü-Cherbi: i follows this part's t; the published parts print Negün-, Öġölen-, with the same men; left, since i follows t spelling.
- Titles: titleEn and part still read 'Chinggis Khan' (published parts write Qahan); outside the fields I was told to touch; for the orchestrator.
- Dozens of 'converb -ing' l renderings, the 'may I' i against 'I will' i in U55: left; U55 i 'I will not let …' is a small inconsistency with U47-50 'may I' that does not alter sense.
- gerlüge (60) 'tent-peg' (Ming 帳房下椿): possibly ger + comitative -lüge; the Ming gloss favours the drafter's reading; left.
- ünijen, qadqu-, quγura-, horči-, möġöre- etc. 'stem inferred' glosses: all rest on the Ming and are marked inferred; left.
- Qorchi's quotation marks in i: opened at U12, U15, U16, U29 … following the units where a new speech or a new Shiratori opening mark begins; the long speech U1-U17 is not wrapped in one pair of quotes in i. Left (house practice in the published parts varies); no change to sense.

## Findings refused or left open (with reason)

- Subject of the 165–174 chain (U23): no longer left as drafted. The recap (U27) puts Temüžin-i before the identical clause baγ̇užu büküi-dür, and §§105–108 has Temüjin camped at Ail-Qaraqana, so Temüjin is now the one camped and the parties come to him. The form still does not decide; i is worded as that reading and n names the other. Remaining doubt (moderate).
- ba at 233 (U31): kept as 'we also—'. The Ming glosses it 也 (not 俺) and the glossary lets ba head a clause as 'we'; no form decides. Remaining doubt, noted in n.
- ba at 281 (U36): kept joined to the preceding sentence as the closing 'we', as at 260 and 266 (俺, each closing a promise with Shiratori's full stop after it); the alternative, that it opens the oath of U37, is now written into n. Remaining doubt.
- qola / oira (461, 463): the 'far / near' claim is removed from `l`, `i`, `n` and the morph and gloss entries. oira = 近 'near' is in the glossary from an earlier part (Ming 近, 根前), but here the Ming gives only 箭名(的), so both words are left untranslated and no pairing is claimed; qola has no Ming gloss anywhere in the sources. Meaning unknown.
- Chinggis Khan in titleEn and part: changed to Chinggis Qahan (published parts: Chinggis Qahan in §§1–6; Qahan for Qaγan throughout). The only 'Khan' in the published parts is one slip in the 100–104 notes, not ours to touch.
- Kimurqa 'stream' against Sengür 'brook' for γoroqan: kept. §§105–108 renders the Kimurqa γorqon 'stream' (and Ail-Qaraqana as in i); §§87–92 has 'brook' for the Sengür. Both are the published parts' own choices.
- Ail-Qaraqana (U23, U27 i) against the glossary's A'il-Qaraqana: kept as Ail-, the spelling of the published i of 105–108.
- jen entry (token jen, eber(i)-jen): not broadened. The glossary's jen entry already lists nouns before -(i)jen with the (i) as Shiratori's accusative or dative (köġün(i)-, ökid(i)-, hüker(i)-, ger-tür(i)-, nidün-dür(i)-); one more noun does not widen its use. Likewise jer (ġür(i)-jer) is covered by 'after mör(i)-', and čiṅgis (Ming here 太祖帝號 / 太祖 against 太祖名) names the same title and is not broadened.
- Qorchi's speech U2–U13 not wrapped in one pair of quotation marks in `i`: left, as in pass 1 (house practice varies); only the U56/U57 pair that closed twice was repaired.
- U15 'If that is true, and I am made to rule the realm' (ünen tein … medeġüilüġesü): left; n already calls it uncertain, and the form does not decide between 'if it is truly so' and a separate affirmation.
- 'Boqdo' in Bodonchar-Boqdo (U2 i, gloss entry): left; no published part prints Boγdo, so there is nothing to match; the γ → q is the drafter's. Remaining doubt (trivial).
- 'alaγčiγ̇ud', 'qoṅγoγčiγ̇ud', 'omoriγ̇ud', 'eres' and the other 'plural -ud / -d' analyses: left; each rests on the Ming (花色, 黄色, 胷每, 家子每) and is marked uncertain where it is.
- Names Taičiγ̇udai Qutu (epithet reading), Nekün-Taiši / Ögölei-Čerbi spelling against the published Negün-/Öġölen-: left as in pass 1.
- gerlüge 'tent-peg': left; 帳房下椿 and the hedged 'sense uncertain' already in the entry.
- abča: left as 'ab- + -ča, ending of uncertain force'; the Ming 將來 does not settle the analysis.
- bolγsau 'a variant of -suγai': left, hedged 'uncertain' in entry and morph.
- alam 'cart-bed / underside': left; Ming 車底 'cart bottom', marked uncertain.
